scope: Ninth-order audit of endogenous experience selection and local-result observability in the unchanged EdgeBench v1 paper and public SForge implementation. AD1/E49 and NR1/E50 are Frontier-Science experiment proposals, not EdgeBench treatments or empirical findings.
source_facts: EdgeBench explicitly contrasts benchmark-organized sequences with one continuous task whose experience stream is endogenous: the agent plans, edits artifacts, submits attempts, receives diagnostics and thereby affects what it learns next.
The EdgeBench inner loop is local and agent-driven, while the outer loop records judge-mediated submissions; for scientific tasks the paper names development splits and validators as local feedback.

EdgeBench defines an effective submission as an agent submission that sets a new best-so-far score. This is an optimization statistic over submitted artifacts, not a scientific completeness criterion for every local experiment.

The public SForge visualizer exposes submission histories, archives, diffs and a downloadable full conversation log, but the public generic harness does not define a task-independent structured schema that guarantees a one-to-one census of every local simulator or instrument action and its positive, null, contradictory, failed or censored outcome.

The approximately 38000-hour raw trajectory corpus and figure-analysis code are not public, so local-result reporting rates or adaptive-design inferential validity cannot be estimated for the EdgeBench headline runs from the public release.

frontier_science_experiments.design: On answer-disjoint procedural worlds, compare fixed randomized or balanced acquisition with agent-adaptive acquisition, and cross the adaptive observations with naive versus policy-aware analysis. Before each outcome, persist the eligible action set, chosen action, acquisition probability or replayable policy state, randomized-exploration probability, stopping rule and evidence lineage. Fail closed on unsupported population contrasts when positivity is absent.

distinct_from.E17: controls repeated adaptive looks at evaluation data rather than inference under an endogenously chosen scientific design
distinct_from.F9_E43: evaluates whether and when feedback is requested rather than whether estimates from selected observations are calibrated
distinct_from.EVI1_E47: accounts for independent evidence units rather than selection probabilities and support of the acquisition policy
distinct_from.V3: tests a fresh final claim but does not retroactively validate confidence intervals computed under an invalid adaptive design

frontier_science_experiments.design: Route every simulator, instrument and data-query action through a trusted append-only event server that durably records intent before revealing the outcome. Compare the objective positive, null, contradictory, failed, timeout and censored result ledger with the agent's submitted claim-evidence package under free-reporting, mandatory all-result-manifest and blinded independent-synthesis arms.

distinct_from.I5_E27: ensures crash-consistent retention and exactly-once accounting but not inclusion of retained unfavorable evidence in a scientific claim
distinct_from.R4: tests revision after contradictory evidence is considered, while NR1 tests whether the evidence is disclosed at all
distinct_from.T1: tests correlated error across investigators rather than selective reporting within one evidence stream
distinct_from.OBS1_E48: tests when latent state is observed rather than which observed local results enter the submitted evidence package

claim_boundary: The source facts do not show that EdgeBench reported scientific effects from adaptively selected observations or that its agents selectively omitted unfavorable local results.
Conversation logs may contain many local tool interactions; the finding is the absence of a guaranteed task-independent structured all-action/result census, not the absence of all local traces.

AD1 and NR1 are motivated by the migration from optimization trajectories to scientific inference and reporting. They are not required to interpret EdgeBench strictly as an optimization or environment-learning benchmark.
Neither AD1 nor NR1 was run when this audit was frozen, and no new Frontier-Science performance, inference-calibration or reporting-completeness result is claimed.
